## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In his comparative study, Masaharu Anesaki also notes variations in the similes found in the Chinese counterparts, including additional similes of an oil lamp and fire following the simile of the infant [Anesaki 1908].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: MA 209 鞞摩那修; T 90 鞞摩肅
- Mentioned in: Cnd 23 Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa

**Sources**

- [Law 1931] Bimala Churn Law, ed., Buddhistic Studies (1931) — Summary of Vekhanasa's discussion with the Buddha on sensual pleasures and connection to the Sakuladāyī discourse.
- [Anesaki 1908] Masaharu Anesaki, The Four Buddhist Āgamas in Chinese: Counterparts in the Pāli Nikāyas (1908) — Observations on parallel passages, reception of the sermon, and distinctive similes in the Chinese counterpart.
